keyFindings: Dual-density design: firm CloudTec outer layer plus softer Helion HF core creates distinctly different heel vs forefoot feel by strike pattern
Excellent cushioning compliance with responsive bounce, especially for midfoot strikers; heel strikers experience firmer initial contact
Technically neutral but mild medial forefoot structure; suitable for runners not requiring significant stability support
Bounce is easily accessible at easy-to-moderate paces but feels somewhat restrictive at faster speeds
Outstanding outsole durability; Pebax-based foam may degrade faster than EVA at high-impact zones over time
Lively and responsive midsole — not soft or mushy; natural feel despite large Helion HF foam insert
Large heel stack provides generous softness for long runs while maintaining energetic ride; Helion HF forefoot adds energy return without instability
Firm heel counter and structured overlays deliver stable support; no wobbling reported even with baggy forefoot fit
Excellent outsole durability with strategic rubber placement; minimal wear after 60km of testing
Versatile for recovery through tempo; best for runners wanting responsiveness and control rather than pure plushness
Responsive and steady ride — balanced underfoot feel that is neither soft nor firm; lacks the trampoline effect of competing super trainers
Partial Pebax midsole feels firm but forgiving; blocky midsole geometry creates clunky transitions rather than smooth cushioning
Excellent heel/midfoot lockdown from engineered upper, but blocky geometry makes the shoe feel heavier and constrains agility
Lacks propulsive reaction — shoe never disappears underfoot as premium trainers should; noticeable presence through each stride
Best for On enthusiasts and heavier runners preferring firmer rides; awkwardly positioned as a $220 premium trainer without true super trainer performance
